findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P2 confidence 100] `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` (also line 195) overwrites concurrent failure increments from the snapshot loaded by `findMany`, so two overlapping scheduler calls that both read zero and fail both store one, undercounting attempts and permitting another attempt after the intended two-failure cutoff; use an atomic increment with an appropriate state guard.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — [P1 confidence 100] `retryCount: { gt: 1, }` deletes successfully scheduled future SMS records when overlapping scheduler calls read a count of one and one succeeds while the other fails, because the failure update is guarded only by `id: reminder.id` and the success update retains the retry count, leaving `scheduled: true` with count two for the next cleanup to erase along with the Twilio reference while the remote message remains scheduled; restrict failure transitions and exhausted-retry cleanup to unscheduled reminders.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — [P2 confidence 100] `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` introduces persistent retry transitions and eventual reminder deletion without any tests or supplied execution evidence, leaving the failure→retry→success and failure→failure→cleanup sequences, the `gt: 1` boundary, and preservation of unrelated reminders unverified for users whose SMS scheduling fails.

packages/prisma/migrations/20240508134359_add_retry_count_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — [P1 confidence 75] Replacing the review-base migration’s empty contents with `ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN     "retryCount" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;` leaves databases that already recorded this migration as applied without the new column because migration deployment skips applied migration identifiers, so the updated scheduler fails on its first `retryCount` query; although the empty file suggests an unshipped placeholder, upgrading an installation of the versioned review base requires a new migration identifier.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — [P2 confidence 100] The unguarded `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({` inside `catch` aborts the entire remaining reminder batch and suppresses the original error log when another cron invocation deletes the in-flight reminder after its scheduled date passes, because both the success update and this recovery update reject for the missing row; although persisting retry counts is necessary, failure to persist one reminder must not escape the per-reminder error boundary and prevent unrelated reminders from being scheduled.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — [P2 confidence 75 advisory] `retryCount: {` with `gt: 1,` in a separate `OR` arm expands this SMS task into deletion of EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders when either channel starts populating the shared retry counter above one, making future channel-specific retry tracking silently destructive; the strongest counterargument is that this patch increments only SMS counters, but that incidental writer behavior does not preserve the SMS ownership boundary in this global deletion predicate, so place `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` outside the `OR`.

goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 — [P1 confidence 100] `retryCount: { gt: 1, }` deletes successfully scheduled future SMS records when overlapping scheduler calls read a count of one and one succeeds while the other fails, because the failure update is guarded only by `id: reminder.id` and the success update retains the retry count, leaving `scheduled: true` with count two for the next cleanup to erase along with the Twilio reference while the remote message remains scheduled; restrict failure transitions and exhausted-retry cleanup to unscheduled reminders.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition issue. Looking at the diff: 1) The deletion query at line 39 uses `OR` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` which would delete ANY reminder with retryCount > 1, regardless of its scheduled status. 2) When SMS scheduling succeeds (line 175-180), the code updates with `referenceId` and `scheduled: true` but does NOT reset retryCount. 3) When scheduling fails (lines 178-185 and 188-196), retryCount is incremented. The race condition: if two scheduler instances process the same reminder, one succeeds (sets scheduled=true, keeps retryCount=1), the other fails (increments to retryCount=2). The next cleanup run would delete this successfully scheduled reminder because retryCount > 1, even though it has a valid Twilio reference. The fix should restrict the `retryCount > 1` deletion to only unscheduled reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — [P2 confidence 100] The unguarded `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({` inside `catch` aborts the entire remaining reminder batch and suppresses the original error log when another cron invocation deletes the in-flight reminder after its scheduled date passes, because both the success update and this recovery update reject for the missing row; although persisting retry counts is necessary, failure to persist one reminder must not escape the per-reminder error boundary and prevent unrelated reminders from being scheduled.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the catch block at line 186-194 contains an unguarded await for prisma.workflowReminder.update(). If this update fails (e.g., because the reminder was deleted by another process), it will throw an exception that escapes the try-catch block for the current reminder iteration. Looking at the code structure, the for loop iterates over reminders, and if an exception escapes the catch block, it would propagate up and potentially abort processing of remaining reminders. The finding accurately describes a real defect where a failure in the error-handling path itself could prevent other reminders from being processed.
